cards.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
cards.note: 1 newton accelerates 1 kg by 1 m/s². Roughly, a 100 g bar of chocolate presses on your hand with about 1 N.

cards.prompt: What is the SI unit of energy?
cards.note: One kilocalorie is about 4,184 joules. The watt, by contrast, measures power, which is energy per second.

cards.prompt: What unit is electrical voltage measured in?
cards.note: Voltage is like the pressure in a water pipe, current like the amount flowing through. Ohm's law links them: V = R × I.

cards.prompt: What unit is electric current measured in?
cards.note: Named after André-Marie Ampère. Power is voltage times current: 230 V × 10 A gives 2,300 W.

cards.prompt: How fast is light in a vacuum, rounded?
cards.note: Exactly 299,792,458 m/s, because since 1983 the metre has been defined by the speed of light. Light from the Sun takes a little over 8 minutes to reach us.

cards.prompt: What is Newton's second law as a formula?
cards.note: Force equals mass times acceleration. A shopping trolley twice as heavy needs twice the force for the same acceleration.

cards.prompt: What is the gravitational acceleration on Earth, rounded?
cards.note: Without air resistance everything falls equally fast, no matter how heavy. By the way, 1.62 m/s² is the value on the Moon.

cards.prompt: What does the unit hertz measure?
cards.note: 1 Hz is one cycle per second. Concert pitch A vibrates at 440 Hz.

cards.prompt: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
cards.note: On a high mountain water boils well below 100 °C because the air pressure is lower. That is why pasta cooks more slowly at altitude.

cards.prompt: Where is absolute zero in degrees Celsius?
cards.note: It equals 0 kelvin. Nothing can get colder, because particles there have the lowest possible energy of motion.

cards.prompt: Which particle in the atom has no electric charge?
cards.note: Protons and neutrons make up the nucleus. The number of protons determines the element, the number of neutrons the isotope.

cards.prompt: Which element has atomic number 1?
cards.note: It is the lightest and most common element in the universe. Stars like the Sun get their energy by fusing hydrogen into helium.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
cards.note: Na comes from the Latin natrium. That is why table salt is written NaCl.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical formula of water?
cards.note: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. H₂O₂, on the other hand, is hydrogen peroxide, a bleach.

cards.prompt: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
cards.note: Air is about 78 percent nitrogen, 21 percent oxygen and just under 1 percent argon. CO₂ is only about 0.04 percent.

cards.prompt: Which element is the most common in the Earth's crust?
cards.note: About 46 percent of the crust is oxygen, bound up in rocks such as quartz (SiO₂). Silicon comes second.

cards.prompt: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
cards.note: Below 7 is acidic, above 7 is alkaline. The scale is logarithmic: pH 5 is ten times more acidic than pH 6.

cards.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
cards.note: Even so, it is not the hottest planet. That is Venus, because its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps the heat.

cards.prompt: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
cards.note: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined. Its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than the Earth.

cards.prompt: How many planets are there in our solar system?
cards.note: Since 2006 Pluto has counted as a dwarf planet, because it has not cleared its orbit of other bodies.

cards.prompt: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
cards.note: It contains an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars. In a few billion years it may merge with the Andromeda Galaxy.

cards.prompt: Which effect makes the sky blue?
cards.note: Short-wavelength blue light is scattered by air molecules much more strongly than red. At sunset the path through the air is so long that mostly red and orange are left.

cards.prompt: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
cards.note: Mitochondria produce ATP, the cell's energy carrier. They have their own DNA, which you inherit only from your mother.

cards.prompt: Where is most of the DNA in a human cell?
cards.note: A small amount also sits in the mitochondria. Bacteria have no nucleus at all; their DNA floats freely in the cell.

cards.prompt: Which molecule carries genetic information?
cards.note: DNA is a double helix built from four bases: A, T, G and C. A always pairs with T, and G always with C.

cards.prompt: How many chromosomes does a normal human body cell have?
cards.note: That is 23 pairs, one set from each parent. Chimpanzees, by the way, have 48.

cards.prompt: Which blood cells carry oxygen?
cards.note: They contain iron-rich haemoglobin, which binds oxygen and gives blood its colour. A red blood cell lives about 120 days.

cards.prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
cards.note: Two atria and two ventricles. The right side pumps blood to the lungs, the left side to the whole body, which is why its wall is thicker.

cards.prompt: Which pigment makes leaves green?
cards.note: Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light and reflects green. In autumn it breaks down and yellow carotenoids show through.

cards.prompt: Which gas do plants release during photosynthesis?
cards.note: Plants build sugar from CO₂, water and light. The oxygen they release comes from the water, not from the CO₂.
